core_obligations: Injections (proof lines 9291-9294): a map is injective precisely when the diagonal is an isomorphism, and the diagonal can be checked after applying the exact stalk functors, so conservativity gives the conclusion.
Surjections (proof lines 9295-9298): the same argument with the codiagonal.

Equality of maps (proof lines 9299-9304): two maps are equal precisely when the inclusion of their equalizer is an isomorphism, and the equalizer is a finite limit, which the exact stalk functors detect.
Limits and colimits (proof lines 9305-9306): the last two assertions follow immediately from the definitions and the exactness remarks at the beginning of the proof.
proof_roadmap: Record that the stalk functors are exact.
Express injectivity, surjectivity and equality of maps as isomorphism statements about finite limits or colimits.
Apply conservativity of the family to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a conservative family of points detects injectivity, surjectivity and equality of maps of sheaves, and that finite limits and colimits may be checked on the stalks (statement lines 9260-9284). The proof is a complete argument: injectivity, surjectivity and equality are each rewritten as the statement that a finite limit or colimit built from the map is an isomorphism, which the exact stalk functors test pointwise and conservativity converts into the assertion (proof lines 9291-9304); the two statements about finite limits and colimits then follow from the definitions and the exactness remarks (proof lines 9305-9306). The non-formal content is the rewriting of the three conditions as isomorphism statements. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
